0.long_answer: German scientists in the late 1920s were among the first to establish a link between tobacco smoking and the development of lung cancer. Lung cancer, which remains one of the deadliest diseases worldwide, was responsible for approximately 1.8 million deaths in 2020. The strong association between smoking and lung cancer has been well documented over the decades, with smoking being identified as the leading risk factor for the disease. This significant mortality rate highlights the public health impact of tobacco use and underscores why lung cancer is a major target for prevention and cessation efforts.
